commit.message:
Apply PR suggestions

1. Updated copyright year for WindowsFileAttributeViews.java and
   CopyAndMove.java.

2. Replaced all instances of `assertTrue()` with equality comparison
   with a call to the newly-introduced `assertEquals()` function.

Incorporate PR suggestions

1. Fix bug in `WindowsFileAttributeViews.setAttributes()`, where the
   order of the arguments was incorrect, causing the last access time
   and the last modified time to be set incorrectly.

2. Skip setting the access time when setting link attributes in the test
   since we don't have a reliable way to check the access time.

3. Minor cosmetic fixes.

Incorporate PR suggestions

1. Renamed `checkCopiedAttributes()` to `checkTargetAttributes()` and
   `checkCopiedLinkAttributes()` to `checkSymLinkAttributes()`.

2. Added an assertion to validate that `sourceAttrs` is indeed a
   symbolic link in `checkSymLinkAttributes()`, since that function
   expects a symbolic link.

3. Ported comments from the code before refactoring and added some new
   ones to clarify individual steps in `checkTargetAttributes()` and in
   `checkSymLinkAttributes()`.

Address PR suggestions

1. Fix directory check in `copySymbolicLink()` to use
   `isDirectoryLink()` instead of `isDirectory()`.

2. Refactored the `copyAndVerify()` function in CopyAndMove.java test so
   that it's clear what's checked for symbolic links versus regular
   files.

3. Added a couple more test cases that exercise copying attributes of
   symbolic links of files and directories.

Remove destination symlink if setting attributes fails

Also fixes what looks like a typo in the handling of failed copying of
attributes when copying directories.  If setting the attributes on the
file or directory fails, then we now remove the copied file or
directory.

Address PR comments

1. Outlined `copyDosAttributes()` back to the original form.

2. Removed code to delete destination symbolic link if there's a failure
   while setting attributes.

Allow copying symbolic links when Developer Mode is enabled on Windows

Prior to this patch, invoking `File.copy()` for copying symbolic links
without following links (i.e. with the flag LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS`)
causes an `AccessDeniedException` exception when the code is run without
elevated privileges when Developer Mode is enabled.  This is because the
`File.copy()` call ultimately invokes the `CopyFileEx()` Win32 API
function, which requires elevated privileges to copy symbolic links.

Instead of copying symbolic links using `CopyFileEx()`, we can instead
recreate the destination symbolic link using the `CreateSymbolicLink()`
Win32 API function, which permits creating symbolic links even without
elevated privileges when `SYMBOLIC_LINK_FLAG_ALLOW_UNPRIVILEGED_CREATE`
is among the flags passed to the function.  This enables the CopyAndMove
test to pass on Windows when Developer Mode is enabled.

The key change in this patch is that `WindowsFileCopy.copy()` now
recognizes when the source file is a symbolic link and if the copy
operation is on the symbolic link itself (rather than the target of the
symbolic link), then it calls `WindowsLinkSupport.createSymbolLink()` to
create a new symbolic link to the target of the original symbolic link.

Validated this patch by running test/jdk tier1, tier2, and tier3 tests
on a FastDebug build.
